LESSON: GRAMMAR 4.3.1 VERBS AND TENSE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it necessary to indicate when an activity takes place?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify verbs in the simple present and simple past tense in a text
2. write sentences using the simple present tense
3. write sentences using the simple past tense

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR 4.3.1 VERBS AND TENSE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR 4.3.1 VERBS AND TENSE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify verbs in the simple present and simple past tense in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify verbs in the simple present and simple past tense in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify verbs in the simple present and simple past tense in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify verbs in the simple present and simple past tense in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write sentences using the simple present tense

What this means
In this part you learn to write sentences using the simple present tense. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write sentences using the simple present tense.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write sentences using the simple present tense. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Write sentences using the simple past tense

What this means
In this part you learn to write sentences using the simple past tense. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write sentences using the simple past tense.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write sentences using the simple past tense. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify verbs in the simple present and simple past tense in a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense to a partner. (skill: write sentences using the simple present tense)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: write sentences using the simple past tense)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify verbs in the simple present and simple past tense in a text.
3. Practise this skill: write sentences using the simple present tense.
4. Practise this skill: write sentences using the simple past tense.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it necessary to indicate when an activity takes place?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify verbs in the simple present and simple past tense in a text.
5. Be able to: write sentences using the simple present tense.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
